paper.title: BB: An R Package for Solving a Large System of Nonlinear Equations and for Optimizing a High-Dimensional Nonlinear Objective Function

code.commit: CRAN archive tarball BB_2009.9-1.tar.gz, DESCRIPTION Version 2009.9-1, Date 2009-10-07
code.archive: sha256 e6b145bda50727838623442e1dc7985b1e9806c68371bf542c600209394ac88e (downloaded by scout 2026-11-26 from the CRAN archive; the tarball is GPL, ~387 KB). Do not use the current BB 2026.1.0, whose results may differ.
code.note: The paper's listing (JSS p. 10-11) is the code to implement: hdp(x) is the Kearfott polynomial system, multiStart(par = p0, fn = hdp, action = "solve"), with p0 <- matrix(runif(900), 300, 3) after setRNG(list(kind = "Mersenne-Twister", normal.kind = "Inversion", seed = 1234)). The archived tests/multiStartHDP.R uses 200 starts (runif(600)) and a different check, so it is not the paper's configuration; the rerun must follow the paper's 300-start listing. The paper calls ans$conv; R's $ partial matching resolves it to ans$converged in the archived code (rerun to confirm).

field: computational mathematics / statistics (nonlinear equation solving, multiple roots)
stack: R (the paper used R 2.9.1 on Windows Vista; the rerun uses a current R with the archived BB 2009.9-1), with packages setRNG (CRAN, for the Mersenne-Twister seed setting) and numDeriv (BB dependency)

claim.location: Section 'Finding multiple roots or multiple local optima -- Function multiStart' (JSS p. 10-11), the text and console output after the hdp listing: 'The sum(ans$conv) gives the number of successful runs (284 in our experiments).'
claim.paper_value: 284 successful runs out of 300 starting values (printed as [1] 284 after R> sum(ans$conv)).
claim.value_check: Read by scout from the JSS PDF (pdftotext -layout of v32i04.pdf, 6 pages) on 2026-11-26: the printed output '[1] 284' and the sentence '(284 in our experiments)' are both on page 11. The 12 unique roots are also printed there, but scout registers only the count.
claim.metric: integer count of converged runs: sum(ans$conv) for multiStart(par = p0, fn = hdp, action = "solve") with p0 <- matrix(runif(900), 300, 3) after the seed 1234 Mersenne-Twister setting

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run: the count is an integer out of 300. The paper warns (p. 9) that floating-point differences across R versions and hardware may change iteration paths, so a pass is a count of 281 to 287 inclusive. Not to be loosened after any run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 1 minute: 300 BBsolve calls on a 3-variable polynomial system (the paper reports 0.15 s for the comparable exponential function over 1000 starts in Table 1).
cost.data_size: None. The multiStart input is generated with runif.
cost.data_licence: No external data. Code: BB (GPL) and setRNG and numDeriv (CRAN, GPL).

why: A deterministic-given-seed integer claim in a 2009 JSS R paper, printed in the text with the seed and RNG kind stated, using the archived CRAN package, and runnable in seconds on CPU.
